rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 and Tables 1-3 - the authors run their own Monte Carlo/EPANET simulations (10,500 per scenario) of the Fuente Palmera on-demand network using 2007 telemetry demand data, and report pressures, power and energy savings for four management scenarios.
rows.notes: The study's own results concern energy and power requirements of an on-demand pressurised network under alternative management (dynamic pressure head, sectoring), showing energy savings up to about 27%. The statements about improved conveyance efficiency (60-70% for open channels vs close to 100% for pressurised networks), reduced water consumption and farmers being able to adopt drip or sprinklers appear only in the Introduction and are attributed to Rodriguez Diaz et al. (2008); they are not a result of this study. No water-loss or conveyance-efficiency measurement is reported. Hence no own evidence on the water-conservation effect claimed in the passage.

rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2-2.5 and Tables 1-3 - own simulation runs of the Fuente Palmera network based on recorded 2007 pumping-station data, reporting energy and power requirements per scenario.
rows.notes: Drip (or any on-farm irrigation method) is not tested, simulated or measured in this study; it is only mentioned in the Introduction as something pressurised networks allow farmers to adopt, citing other work. The study's own results are about energy requirements of network management scenarios (sectoring, dynamic pressure head), not about drip or water conservation. Technology mismatch: the study concerns on-demand pressurised network management, not drip irrigation.

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is a simulation-based analysis (EPANET/Monte Carlo) of energy saving scenarios for an on-demand pressurised irrigation district in Spain; it reports no water-saving or conveyance-efficiency results of its own, and the water-related claims in the passage derive from works it cites (Rodriguez Diaz et al. 2008), not from its own findings. The model output is not compared with measured energy data, though input demand is taken from telemetry records.
